security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives. Four detections mistake Markdown backticks and Motoko code fences for shell execution, while the URL is a documentation link. No evidence of prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: There is the prefabricated module `mo:caffeineai-http-outcalls/outcall.mo` that that cannot be modif

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 22 uses Markdown backticks to format a Motoko module path. It does not invoke Ruby, a shell, or any external command.
Line 24 opens a fenced documentation block containing Motoko interface declarations. The block is reference text and contains no shell execution.
Line 46 only closes the preceding Markdown code fence. It cannot execute a command.
Line 50 opens a fenced Motoko usage example with a filepath annotation. It is documentation syntax, not a Ruby or shell command.
The hardcoded URL is the destination of a Markdown link identifying Caffeine AI. It is not used as an HTTP outcall target and sends no skill data.

content.user_title: Build Backend HTTP Outcalls in Motoko
content.value_statement: Backend canisters need a reliable way to call external APIs. This skill shows how to use the Caffeine AI outcall module for GET and POST requests.
actual_capabilities: Explains how backend canisters make HTTP GET and POST requests.
Documents the prefabricated Caffeine AI outcall module interface.
Defines the request header and transformation callback types.
Shows a Motoko GET request with the provided transform helper.
Clarifies that JSON parsing should be handled by the frontend.
limitations: The guidance applies to backend canisters, not frontend requests.
The prefabricated outcall module cannot be modified.
Motoko does not directly support the described JSON parsing workflow.
POST support is described, but only GET has a complete usage example.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Backend GET Outcall
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how this skill performs a backend GET request to [API URL]. Identify the import, transform callback, and request call.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the basic request flow before editing a canister.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a GET Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Motoko backend function that sends a GET request to [API URL] with [headers] and uses the provided transform callback.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a specific read-only API integration.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a POST Outcall
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a POST outcall from a backend canister to [service]. Specify headers, body handling, transform usage, and response processing boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a backend request that submits data.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Outcall Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare backend GET and POST integration options for [service]. Recommend function boundaries, reusable headers, transform handling, and frontend JSON parsing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate a more complex service integration.

output_examples.input: How should my backend canister call a weather API?
output_examples.output: Import the prefabricated outcall module, define a query transform callback, and send a GET request from a backend function.

output_examples.input: Can the canister post data and parse the JSON response?
output_examples.output: The module supports POST requests with headers, a body, and a transform callback. Send JSON responses to the frontend for parsing.

output_examples.input: What parts of the outcall module can I customize?
output_examples.output: Keep the prefabricated module unchanged. Customize your backend functions, request URL, headers, body, and response workflow.

best_practices: Keep HTTP outcall logic in backend canister functions.
Use the provided transform helper through a query callback.
Validate request targets and avoid sending secrets to untrusted services.
anti_patterns: Do not modify the prefabricated outcall module.
Do not assume Motoko directly parses JSON responses in this workflow.
Do not pass untrusted URLs directly into backend outcall functions.

faq.question: Which HTTP methods does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers GET and POST requests from backend canisters.

faq.question: Can I use this guidance in the frontend?
faq.answer: No. The documented outcalls are performed by the backend canister.

faq.question: Can I modify the outcall module?
faq.answer: No. The Caffeine AI outcall module is prefabricated and cannot be modified.

faq.question: How are responses transformed?
faq.answer: Define a query callback that delegates to the module's provided transform helper.

faq.question: How should I parse JSON responses?
faq.answer: Send JSON to the frontend for parsing because this workflow does not directly support Motoko JSON parsing.

faq.question: Does the skill include a POST example?
faq.answer: It documents the POST function signature and states that usage is analogous, but it provides a complete example only for GET.
